chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When a group of people gather upon a hunt, and they are in Ihram during its hunting, or they eat from it, so upon each one of them is its price.

key_terms.قِيمَتُهُ: Its price/compensation (the value of the game to be paid as fidya)
key_terms.مُحْرِمُونَ: Those in the state of Ihram, pilgrims in their consecrated state

ai.seo_question: What is the compensation for a group of pilgrims who hunt together while in Ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that the compensation (qimah) for hunting game while in Ihram is assessed individually per person rather than collectively, a key distinction in Shia fiqh regarding joint liability. It underscores the principle that each pilgrim bears the burden of their own act of consumption or capture, reflecting the broader legal maxim of individual accountability in ritual violations. This ruling is particularly significant for understanding the practical application of Surah Al-Ma'idah's injunctions on hunting during pilgrimage.
